about: Financial terms FinanzApp uses with one meaning each. Every translation keeps these distinctions; the export script attaches the terms a key contains. Add a term before translating a new concept.

terms.note: Money spent and recorded. Never 'payment' (a payment settles a card or a debt).
Money received. Uncountable in English: '3 income entries', not '3 incomes'.
Any recorded expense, income or transfer. Not 'movement'.
Between the person's own accounts; never spending or income.
What the app computed from the records. Never 'bank balance'.
Recorded liquid money in one currency; excludes cards and debts. Never 'net worth'.
Monthly ceiling, overall or per category.
A credit card tracked as a liability.
The credit-card statement for one cycle.
Last day purchases enter a statement.
Last day to pay a statement or a debt.
Money the person owes (debo) — see 'cobro' for money owed to them.
Receiving money someone owed the person.
A card balance in the person's favour.
A scheduled expense or income rule; scheduled is not paid.
One part of a purchase paid in several months.
Built-in names are translated; the person's own names never are.
A place the person keeps money (cash, bank, wallet), tracked manually.
A JSON file the person exports and imports.
Voids a record; it can be restored ('recuperar' → 'restore'). Never 'delete'.
An Assistant proposal that is not saved until confirmed.
Product name of the in-app assistant; capitalised.
Where an expense happened; user data is never translated.
An ISO 4217 currency, a property of an account (never of the device, the language or the region). Named by CLDR in the interface language; 'moneda' is never 'divisa'.
The ISO 4217 alphabetic code (ARS, USD, JPY), shown as is in every language; never translated or replaced by a symbol.
The short sign before an amount ($, US$, €, JP¥, or the code when CLDR has none). A bare $ is the peso only in Argentina.
The currency's own minor-unit digits (JPY none, KWD three). Never 'centavos' for a currency other than ARS/USD.
The integer the ledger stores (cents, yen, fils). Never shown to the person as such.
A dated rate between two currencies, with its source. Never invented; none exists before Producto 24C.
The future currency of consolidated reports (24C); separate from an account's currency and from the region.
What was actually debited in the account's currency. Distinct from an original foreign amount and from an estimate.
Computed from a reference rate, not debited. Always labelled as such; never counted as a balance.
A total or amount beyond the exact integer range. Shown explicitly (a dash or a sentence), never rounded or dropped.
